title: The Beholder's Share
content: The artist only does half of the work of a painting. The other half is done by the viewer.Honore Daumier's sketch of the Salon:"THE VISITOR: – Just look at this senseless arrangement… and these colours!… hideous!THE ARTIST: – Cretin of a bourgeois… buzz off!This idea is sometimes referred to as the "beholder's share," a term popularized by art historiansErnst Gombrich(1909-2001) andErnst Kris(1900-1957).The beholder is the partner of the creator and is deeply involved in the process of bringing an image to life.Arnold Böcklin,Isle of the DeadImages that are more open-ended in their interpretation involve the viewer in a particularly strong way. Ernst Kris said 'Great works are great because they are ambiguous."Eric Kandel discusses the topic of the beholder's share in this episode ofBig Think.----
